p: Skating is brilliant fun, but it's only a couple of hours at most, which leaves plenty of time to explore one of the south coast's most underrated towns. Gosport is packed with naval history, and the Royal Navy Submarine Museum is a real highlight, where you can learn about life under the waves and see historic submarines up close. Explosion, the museum of naval firepower, tells the story of weapons and the people who made them, and both make a great follow-up to an active morning on the ice.

If you want a bit of sea air, Stokes Bay offers a long stretch of shingle beach with views over the Solent to the Isle of Wight. And the Gosport Ferry is a fun little hop across the harbour to Portsmouth, where Gunwharf Quays and the Spinnaker Tower are close to the landing.

Back at the rink, it's worth remembering that ice is cold and wet, so pack sensibly. Gloves, a jumper and trousers that won't mind a damp patch are all you need. Leave valuables at home or tucked safely in a zipped pocket, as anything that falls out mid-glide tends to slide a surprisingly long way.
Beginners should start near the barrier and build up slowly. There's no shame in a few laps hanging on, and you'll be amazed how quickly confidence builds once you've got the hang of the glide.
